cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a complete backstrap loom with a section of weft-brocaded textile in burgundy, yellow and green wool on cotton, plus the weaver's mecapal strap — backstrap-loom brocade weaving is a hallmark craft of the Tzotzil Maya of Chiapas. The claimed category "instruments" is wrong (this is weaving equipment, not a musical instrument), but that mislabeling doesn't affect ethnic attribution.

physical.title: loom
physical.summary: Backstrap loom; made of wood; with a section of weft-brocaded textile in burgundy, yellow and green wool on white cotton ground already woven. Basic construction: 1) twined rope to wrap around tree; 2) dowel at top, wrapped with green "heading cords"; 3) dowel twined through weft threads; 4) dowel twined through weft threads; 5) flat piece of wood with tapered ends; 6) thin flat piece of wood with tapered ends; 7) dowel with "heading cord" wrapped around it; 8) weaver's strap (mecapal in Spanish) plaited from vegetable fibre for strapping around weaver's waist.
